sections.h2: Which Brandenburg offices matter for a Meade County tax bill?
sections.html:
Most of the work happens in two suites at 516 Hillcrest Drive. The assessor's side, formally the Property Valuation Administration (PVA), sits in Suite 3 and answers at (270) 422-2178 on weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Suite 14 is the Sheriff's Office, where payments are taken, at (270) 422-4937.

Value is one office's business and collection is the other's. Take exemption and value questions to Suite 3, and take a bill in hand to Suite 14. The County Clerk becomes involved only after April 15, once unpaid bills have transferred.

sections.h2: How and when do Meade County residents pay?
sections.html:
Pay the Sheriff. The Sheriff mailed the 2026 bills on October 30, 2026, a Friday, and a notice dated November 4 conceded that many owners still had not received theirs. It directed them to an online lookup of 2026 tax information so the amount could be checked while the mail caught up.

  • A 2 percent discount is available under KRS 134.015 for settling in full by November 1. Because the 2026 bills only left October 30, ask the Sheriff which dates apply; the law permits a different schedule when mailing is delayed.
  • Between then and New Year's Eve, no discount and no penalty.
  • January brings 5 percent.
  • After January it is 10 percent.
  • Collection ends April 15, and in 2026 the counter took its last walk-in payment at 4:30 in the afternoon.

Personal checks are refused for the last two weeks of each collection season, so late payers need cash, a card, a money order or a cashier's check. The office describes this as a yearly custom, with personal checks accepted again earlier in future seasons.

sections.h2: What does a typical Meade County house owe?
sections.html:
Census reports $207,900 for the typical owned home, more than McCracken County's $188,100. The state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents on each $100 works out to about $220.37 for Frankfort on that house. Separate levies from the county, the school district and special districts are added. Monthly ownership costs run $1,344 with a mortgage and $462 without.

Between 1950 and 1960 the head count almost doubled, and growth has continued:

The July 2025 estimate of 30,699 is 2.3 percent above the 2020 figure. Typical rent is $1,026, typical household income is $74,355, and 165 new-construction permits were issued in 2025. Payroll jobs climbed 6.2 percent from 2022 to 2023, reaching 3,633 across 362 employers, and shoppers spent about $305 million in stores during 2022.

The county has 11,007 households averaging 2.72 people and 12,666 housing units. About 87.6 percent of residents stayed in the same house through the year before the survey, a lower share than in McLean or McCreary counties. Children under 18 were 25.5 percent of the 2020 population, with a median age of 38.4. The 2020 census counted 11,943 housing units, 7.5 percent of them vacant, and 27.2 percent of occupied homes were rented. That share matters to a seller with a tenant in place, who should settle access for showings with the tenant before listing the house.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Meade County?
sections.html:
Yes. Kentucky offers a $49,100 cut in assessed value, good for the 2025 and 2026 years, to homeowners who are 65 or older or totally disabled. Applied to the $207,900 median, it leaves $158,800 to tax and brings the state's piece down to roughly $168.33.

The Meade County PVA announced May 22, 2026 as the date by which an application would make the November bill. It is behind us now. Someone turning 65 later should call the office to learn the matching date. Early filing, the PVA says, helps taxing districts plan. For age, the office accepts a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. A disability claim rests on a total-disability finding and is renewed annually, except for service-connected veterans and anyone with a permanent determination from Social Security or state retirement.

sections.h2: How does a Meade County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
The PVA conference comes first, and staff use it to show how your value was built. After it, the state calendar governs:

  • Roll viewing lasts 13 days, beginning the first Monday in May.
  • Lodge the appeal at the County Clerk's office before closing on the next business day.
  • Gather land and building records: insurance, construction costs, comparable sale listings.
  • Attend the local board of assessment appeals, convened roughly a month after viewing for up to five days.

You may record the hearing. Should the board's number exceed your claim after bills have gone out, a supplemental bill covers the gap.

sections.h2: What if Meade County tax is still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
A sale does not wipe it out. Any bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff becomes a certificate in the Clerk's hands, a lien is filed, and interest of 1 percent a month begins. Under KRS 134.420 the lien may last 11 years under any owner.

Two notices come from the county attorney, one inside 30 days of the transfer and one inside 60. The Clerk sets a sale 90 to 135 days out, and a certificate buyer may add substantial fees. Request a payoff from the Sheriff before April 15 and from the Clerk after it, and have the closing agent pay from proceeds.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Meade County?
sections.html:
Created in 1823, Meade County covers 325 square miles, and the Ohio River runs along its 56-mile northern line, facing Indiana. Karst plains riddled with sinkholes cover much of the land, while the northwest rests on a plateau behind the Dripping Springs Escarpment. Brandenburg is the seat. Ekron and Muldraugh are the county's other cities, with Doe Valley and Fort Knox listed as census-designated places. Hardin County shares Fort Knox, and Meade is part of the Louisville metro area, close to the job centers at Elizabethtown and Fort Knox.

Meade County Schools, with Meade County High School, teaches most children. Families living on the Fort Knox base are zoned to the Defense Department's schools instead. Eastern time applies here, while neighbors Breckinridge County and Perry County, Indiana, are on Central.

Workers travel a mean 33.0 minutes to their jobs. Owners occupy 74.1 percent of homes, and 91.5 percent of households subscribe to broadband. Veterans number 2,790, and 91.0 percent of adults finished high school. Poverty stands at 9.8 percent, against 13.9 percent in McCracken County. Sinkholes are common in this terrain, and a house with one or with deferred repairs can stall a conventional sale. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is can close without those fixes. Wikipedia's county photographs show sinkholes near Hog Wallow, looking toward Ekron, a reminder that ground conditions vary from one Meade County parcel to the next, so a buyer's inspection may ask about them.

faqs.q: Where do I pay the Meade County Sheriff?
faqs.a: Visit 516 Hillcrest Drive, Suite 14, in Brandenburg, or call (270) 422-4937. Suite 3, the PVA, cannot accept payments.

faqs.q: When does the Meade County Sheriff stop taking personal checks?
faqs.a: From two weeks before April 15 onward. Cash, cards, money orders and cashier's checks remain acceptable.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 homestead filing cutoff in Meade County?
faqs.a: May 22, 2026, for a place on the November bill. It has passed, so ask the PVA what the next cutoff is.

faqs.q: How much state tax falls on a $207,900 Meade County house?
faqs.a: Close to $220.37 on the 2025 state rate, before county and school levies.

faqs.q: What becomes of Meade County bills left open after April 15?
faqs.a: The Clerk receives them as certificates of delinquency and files a lien. Interest accrues at 1 percent monthly, and the Clerk may schedule a sale within 90 to 135 days.
